record_body:
Account Summary
- Regulated regional bank. Vendor risk / security review is gating. Strong preference for Private deployment (customer VPC). They are explicitly not comfortable with “hosted API” for production data.
- Workload: internal agent for knowledge base + policy Q&A; some summarization of customer comms; expected to add embeddings + reranking later.

Firmographics / Procurement
- Procurement path: vendor risk + security questionnaire -> architecture review -> POC in non-prod VPC -> contract.
- Legal note from customer: wants language that Redwood does not have access to plaintext and that they control master keys (CMK) for Private.

Ownership
- AE: Maya Chen
- SE: Simran Kaur (ref arch + security)
- Internal stakeholders pulled in: Marcus Lin (Security), Hanae Suzuki (Private templates), Elliot Price (Docs)

Current Stage Notes (Evaluation)
- Customer is in security evaluation; technical buy-in is “conditional” on KMS + audit evidence.
- They asked for: (a) formal key rotation procedure, (b) audit event list for key lifecycle + encrypt/decrypt failures, (c) statement on KMS failure modes / resilience.

Security / Compliance Requirements (most important)
1) Customer-managed KMS (Private)
- They want customer-owned KEK/CMK. Redwood should not own the root keys for their deployment.
- Need explicit provider support statement: AWS KMS primary; they asked if Azure Key Vault supported (answer: roadmap/limited; keep wording careful).
- Strong requirement: deterministic key selection and no “silent drift” of key versions during rollouts/upgrades.

2) Key rotation
- Rotation cadence requested: “at least annual” for scheduled rotation; plus emergency rotation within days if compromise suspected.
- They want to know:
  - Expected downtime (target: none / minimal)
  - Whether rotation requires re-encrypting stored artifacts vs dual-read window
  - How rollback works if new key has policy mistake
- Customer quote (from SE): “Rotation is a control test for us. We need a repeatable procedure and proof it happened.”

3) Audit logging / evidence
- Must have audit events showing:
  - key id / key version used (at least KEK/CMK reference)
  - rotation initiation and completion markers
  - decrypt failures with reason category (timeout/throttle/AccessDenied/DisabledKey)
  - breakglass access events (who/when/why) if ever used
- Retention: they asked for 1 year minimum, prefer 18–24 months. (We should confirm what is standard vs add-on.)
- Customer asked if they can export audit logs to their SIEM (Splunk). We said yes via standard export/forwarding patterns; follow up with specifics.

4) Identity / access
- SSO/SAML for admin console is required.
- Private operator access: they want clear separation between customer ops vs Redwood support, and “no standing access”. Breakglass only.

5) Data residency
- They prefer US-only regions; no cross-region failover that would move data outside US without explicit opt-in.

Performance / Scale (high level)
- Latency target mentioned: p95 < 1.5s for short chat responses in internal network; throughput not final.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate; they care more about predictability + auditability than absolute lowest cost.

Activity Timeline (recent)
- 2026-01-14: Created account after inbound from security@northlake + intro via partner.
- 2026-01-28: Discovery call (SE notes: Private VPC is non-negotiable; strong KMS focus).
- 2026-02-10: Security review call transcript captured (Fireflies ff_9b3f2a1d). Main topics: customer-managed KMS, rotation cadence, audit evidence, KMS outage behavior.
- 2026-02-12: Sent initial security FAQ + draft answers; customer replied asking for “formal procedure doc” (Gmail thread_19c2f0d8).
- 2026-02-18: Internal sync w/ Security Eng (Marcus/Hanae) on wording: what we can commit to now vs post-project rollout.
- 2026-02-20: SE shared draft “KMS rotation customer Q&A” from Drive and promised a cleaner operator-facing rotation procedure for Private.

Open Questions / To Confirm
- Which cloud: customer said “AWS first”, but they have some Azure footprint. Need to confirm for POC.
- Whether their key policy requires explicit deny statements / external key store constraints.
- Whether they require HSM-backed keys (KMS HSM) or standard KMS is acceptable.

Next Steps (internal)
- Provide customer-facing pack:
  - Rotation procedure (Private) + step-by-step prerequisites (IAM/KMS) + validation checklist
  - Audit event list (schema-level) and retention statement
  - Failure-mode expectations: timeouts/throttling/AccessDenied/disabled key; what happens to reads/writes; operator runbook highlights
- Schedule follow-up with their cloud security (KMS/IAM owner) + our Security lead Marcus Lin.

Risk / Blocker Notes
- Risk: if we can’t provide clear “rotation complete” definition + evidence, vendor risk may stall or require contractual commitments we can’t meet.
- Risk: customer is sensitive to any language implying Redwood can access/rotate their keys without customer action in Private.
